source: bine deci sa-ti zic cum am facut eu, practic cand ai nevoie de performanta mai buna in app nu te mai bizui doar pe Kotlin ca prea incet pe unele chestii, asa ca bagi cod native prin NDK, adica scri in C sau C++, pui fisierele alea in folder-ul jni, faci un CMakeLists.txt sa-ti compileze, apoi in gradle activezi externalNativeBuild si setezi abiFilters sa fie arm64-v8a si armeabi-v7a ca sa mearga pe toate telefoanele, si acolo unde vrei sa chemi functiile din C declari metode external fun in Kotlin cu keyword-ul native si le legi prin JNI cu numele pachetului exact, eu la al meu de scanning am asa facut si merge de 3 ori mai repede, doar nu uita ca daca crapa in codul native nu primesti stack trace normal ci tre sa folosesti ndk-stack ca sa vezi ce-ai stricat, si da-mi mesaj daca te blochezi la linking ca acolo m-am blocat si eu jumatate de zi
target: okay so let me tell you how I did it, basically when you need better performance in the app you don't just rely on Kotlin anymore because it's too slow for some things, so you put native code through the NDK, meaning you write in C or C++, you put those files in the jni folder, you make a CMakeLists.txt to compile it, then in gradle you enable externalNativeBuild and set abiFilters to be arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a so it works on all phones, and where you want to call functions from C you declare external fun methods in Kotlin with the native keyword and link them through JNI with the exact package name, I did this for my scanning one and it runs 3 times faster, just don't forget that if it crashes in the native code you don't get a normal stack trace but you have to use ndk-stack to see what you broke, and message me if you get stuck on linking because that's where I got stuck for half a day too
